text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The message sent by President Farooq Leghari to both the houses of Parliament calling for appropirate legislation for the eradication of corruption will come up for discussion in the Senate on Wednesday.

- An officer at the Indian High Commission A.C Sinha, who was arrested on Monday on a charge of espionage in Islamabad, has been declared a persona non grata and asked to leave Pakistan by October 4, officials said.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange will do normal business next Friday and observe Sunday as a weekly holiday.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto arrived in New York on Monday night on a four day visit to the United States.

- The Senate has passed a unanimous resolution condemning the oppressive policies of Israel and calling for reversal of all illegal measuers taken by Tel Aviv including opening of the tunnel near Al-Aqsa Mosque and action against unarmed civilians.
- Pakistan and Australia have signed a new air services agreement which enables Islamabad to re-establish airlinks with Canberra after a gap of almost 30 years.
- The Corporate Law Authroity has approved the prospectus of Japan Power Generation Ltd for the public issue of capital worth 138 million rupees.

- Pakistan is unlikely to cut its fiscal deficit to four percent of gross domestic product as agreed with the International Monetary Fund despite showing strong economic growth, Crosby Securities said in a report.

- The World Bank, admitting the fact that 34 projects having letter of support for the thermal power generation would result in far too much power if materialised, has stressed the government to accept them to avoid serious backlash of investors.
- Pakistan and Tajikistan have signed a memorandum of understanding for the construction of a highway trade route between the two countries.
